clue.text: Singer's No 1 hit recalled a day around mid-January

indicators.note: around has the reversed word wrapping the next piece
recalled is taken as called back, so the word for hit runs backwards

parts.note: number one is the Roman numeral I
to slap is to hit

indicators.note: mid- asks for the central letter of the month's name

parts.note: Mon is short for Monday, a day

explanation.surface: A tribute to a singer whose chart-topping single is remembered on a winter's day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' reverses I SLAP to PALSI; 'around' wraps that round U, the middle letter of January ('mid'). The 's is 'is'; a day is MON, Monday.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul Simon is the American singer-songwriter, once of Simon and Garfunkel.

clue.text: Test bed involves one

indicators.note: involves means wraps around, so the garden word takes in the numeral

parts.note: a plot is a bed of ground for planting
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A trial of a bed which includes one item, perhaps in a garden.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilot is a trial run, as in a pilot scheme tested before wider use.

clue.text: Released from custody, but unlikely to go off?

definitions.meaning: a suspect let go without being formally accused
a battery or weapon without a charge in it will not fire or explode

explanation.surface: Someone let out of a police station is no longer a danger.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncharged means both not accused of a crime and not loaded with electricity or explosive.

clue.text: Most optimistic Muslim is French

parts.note: a Sunni is a member of the largest branch of Islam
est is French for is

explanation.surface: A claim that a Muslim of France is especially hopeful.
explanation.definitionFit: Sunniest, superlative of sunny, describes the most cheerful, upbeat disposition.

clue.text: Encountered character at last in French city

parts.note: to have met someone is to have encountered them
Z is the final character of the alphabet

explanation.surface: Finally meeting a fictional character in a city in France.
explanation.definitionFit: Metz is a city in north-eastern France, in Lorraine.

clue.text: TV programme shot in bush region

indicators.note: shot here means ruined or broken, so these letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: A television show filmed out in the bush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' rearranges BUSH REGION. The surface fits: Neighbours is an Australian soap opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Neighbours is a long-running Australian television soap opera set on Ramsay Street.

clue.text: This language not entirely acceptable?

indicators.note: not entirely says only part of the words This language is used, the letters inside them

explanation.surface: A disapproving remark about someone's choice of words.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines and builds: the letters run across 'This language', and the vocabulary in question is not wholly acceptable.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang is very informal vocabulary, often thought unfit for formal use.

clue.text: Pull broken down used car at the front, with minimum of energy

indicators.note: broken down means the letters of used have fallen apart and are rebuilt
at the front takes just the opening letter of car

parts.note: E is the symbol for energy, and as a single letter it is the least of the word

explanation.surface: A breakdown recovery truck pulls a decrepit second-hand car with little power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken down' rearranges USED into SEDU.
explanation.definitionFit: To pull someone, in British slang, is to attract and win them over romantically.

clue.text: A look round American battle site

indicators.note: round means the old exclamation encircles the abbreviation

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look!

explanation.surface: Taking a look around a US battlefield.
explanation.definitionFit: The Alamo, a mission in Texas, was the site of the 1836 siege and battle.

clue.text: Proceeds east, entering residential area of Newcastle

indicators.note: entering means the compass letter goes inside the suburb's name

parts.note: Gosforth is a suburb of Newcastle upon Tyne in north-east England

explanation.surface: Someone travels east into a Newcastle neighbourhood.
explanation.walkthrough: GOSFORTH is a suburb of Newcastle upon Tyne, a city in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: To go forth is to set out or advance, a formal way of saying proceeds.

clue.text: Lord once missing rest rooms, reportedly?

indicators.note: reportedly says the two words for lavatories are heard, not spelt

parts.note: loo and can are both slang for a lavatory

explanation.surface: A puzzled query about a peer who vanished, tied oddly to public toilets.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord Lucan disappeared in 1974 after his children's nanny was murdered and was never found. LOO and CAN are British and American slang for a toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: The 7th Earl Lucan famously vanished in 1974, a peer who went missing for good.

clue.text: Drier that conked out, not top quality

indicators.note: a machine that has conked out is broken, so these letters are broken up and remade

explanation.surface: A complaint about a cheap tumble dryer that has broken down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conked out' rearranges the letters of DRIER and THAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Third-rate means of poor quality, ranking well below the best.

clue.text: With time to party endlessly, is following rock band

indicators.note: following puts the word is after what comes before it
endlessly means the word for party loses its final letter

parts.note: a rave is a large dance party

explanation.surface: Someone with time to spare keeps partying after a rock band's gig.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' trims RAVE to RAV.
explanation.definitionFit: Travis is a Scottish rock group, known for songs such as Why Does It Always Rain on Me?

clue.text: Tick name of Russian playwright, some say

indicators.note: some say indicates a sound-alike: the dramatist's surname heard spoken

parts.note: Anton Chekhov wrote The Seagull and The Cherry Orchard

explanation.surface: An instruction to mark off a famous Russian dramatist's name, perhaps on a reading list.
explanation.definitionFit: To check off an item on a list is to tick it as done.

clue.text: Island very keen on a vehicle that's petrol-filled?

parts.note: mad about or mad on means very keen on

indicators.note: filled means the fuel word goes inside the words for a vehicle

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
gas is the American word for petrol

explanation.surface: A query about an island fond of fuelled-up cars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'very keen on' is MAD as in 'mad on'; GAS is American for petrol, and 'filled' sets it inside A CAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Madagascar is a large island nation off the south-east coast of Africa.

clue.text: When many people holiday on the world's oceans, principally?

parts.note: the high seas are the open oceans beyond any country's waters

explanation.surface: A musing on when most holidaymakers take to sea cruises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'principally' is a playful link, hinting that the open oceans mostly make the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: High season is the peak period of the year for tourism, when holidays are most popular.

clue.text: Former officer, outwardly injured, is to speak to followers

indicators.note: outwardly means the word for injured goes round the outside

parts.note: hurt means injured
old means former
CO stands for commanding officer

explanation.surface: A retired, wounded officer addresses his troops.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold court is to hold forth to an admiring circle, like a monarch to courtiers.

clue.text: Who wants leading parts in street theatre and rep?

definitions.text: Who wants leading parts in street theatre and rep?

indicators.note: leading parts asks for the first letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: Who covets the top roles in performances on the street and in repertory?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: the first letters of street, theatre, and, rep, and the performer craving lead roles.
explanation.definitionFit: A star is the principal performer, the one who expects to take the lead roles.

clue.text: The Times — as seen in Perth?

definitions.text: The Times — as seen in Perth?

parts.words: The Times — as seen in Perth?
parts.note: the London newspaper's old nickname, read here as 'the down-under-er', a paper seen in Australia

explanation.surface: A question about how a British daily newspaper appears in an Australian city.
explanation.walkthrough: The Times was nicknamed 'The Thunderer'; split as TH-UNDER-ER it hints at Perth, in Western Australia, down under.
explanation.definitionFit: The Thunderer is a traditional nickname for The Times newspaper of London.

clue.text: Having good reason to expect degree, learner's relaxed

parts.note: to be in for something is to have it coming
MA is a Master of Arts degree
L is the learner plate on a British car

explanation.surface: A student hopes for a degree and is calm about it.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after learner is 'is', linking wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal means casual, without ceremony, much like relaxed.

clue.text: Youngster with a Russian car

parts.note: a lad is a young boy

explanation.surface: A young man owns a car made in Russia.
explanation.definitionFit: Lada is a Russian make of car, famous for the boxy Riva.

clue.text: Mentioned food one rejected? That's revolting, I agree

indicators.note: Mentioned says the word for food is spoken, so it is heard as a homophone

parts.note: fare is food and drink served
a diner pushing away one more helping of something nasty cries 'Enough!'

explanation.surface: Someone turns away a dish they find disgusting, and a companion concurs.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair enough is a conversational phrase of acceptance, conceding a point is reasonable.

clue.text: Cooked meat: something extra cut for picnic basket

parts.note: ham is cured and cooked pork

indicators.note: cut means the end is chopped off the word for something extra

parts.note: a perk is an extra benefit

explanation.surface: Packing cooked meat and some extra treat for a picnic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' trims PERK to PER.
explanation.definitionFit: A hamper is a wicker basket with a lid, used to carry food for a picnic.

clue.text: Movie actors not on set?

parts.note: the cast is the troupe of actors in a production
actors not on set are away from it

explanation.surface: A query about a film whose performers are absent from the studio.
explanation.definitionFit: Cast Away is the 2000 film starring Tom Hanks as a man marooned on an island.

clue.text: Material stood out? The opposite

parts.note: the opposite of stood is sat
the opposite of out is in

explanation.surface: A puzzle about a fabric that was conspicuous, or perhaps not.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The opposite' says to swap each of 'stood out' for its contrary: SAT and IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Satin is a smooth, glossy fabric, a kind of cloth or material.

clue.text: Surprise about Democrat currently moving to the left

indicators.note: in an across entry, moving to the left means the assembled pieces are read backwards

parts.note: re means about, as in a letter heading
D is the abbreviation for a Democrat in US politics
now means at present, currently

explanation.surface: Political astonishment at a Democrat who is shifting leftwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving to the left' reverses REDNOW.
explanation.definitionFit: Wonder is amazement, the feeling of surprise at something unexpected.

clue.text: Out of practice, rugby guy's no amateur

parts.note: RU stands for Rugby Union

indicators.note: no amateur means the A, short for amateur, is removed

parts.note: a guy is a rope stay supporting a tent or mast

explanation.surface: A rugby player who is a professional has lost some sharpness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no amateur' drops A from STAY, leaving STY.
explanation.definitionFit: Being rusty means a skill has deteriorated through lack of use.

clue.text: Pellet — that will do for garden pest

definitions.meaning: a bullet or piece of lead shot
a shell-less mollusc that eats plants

explanation.surface: Using a pellet gun to deal with a garden pest.
explanation.definitionFit: Slug means both a bullet and a slimy mollusc that ravages gardens.

clue.text: Drastic cut in play not expected?

indicators.note: drastic suggests violent upheaval, so these letters are turned upside down and remade

explanation.surface: An unexpected, severe cut made to a stage play's script.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drastic' rearranges CUT IN PLAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Untypical means unrepresentative of the norm, so out of line with what is expected.

clue.text: Stretches of water in some resorts

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the words some resorts

explanation.surface: Lakes and pools to be found in certain holiday resorts.
explanation.definitionFit: Meres are lakes or ponds, a word especially common in northern English place names.

clue.text: Singer's note right, after short number

indicators.note: after places the abbreviation for right behind the short number

parts.note: te is a note of the sol-fa scale
no. is the short form of number

explanation.surface: A vocalist hits the right note after a brief song.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenor is a male singer with a high voice.

clue.text: Developed urge to attend subversive rally often

indicators.note: developed signals the letters of urge are worked into a new form
subversive suggests overturning, so the letters of rally are upset

explanation.surface: A growing impulse to join a rebellious demonstration again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Developed' turns URGE into REGU; 'subversive' turns RALLY into LARLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Regularly means at frequent, repeated intervals, much like often.
